content: The Founder sits back down at the table for the first time since lunch. 'Cut what we can't do well in 30 days. I'd rather ship six things properly than nine things badly.'

Head of Product goes down the column quickly. 'CUT: a pot in the box. CUT: shouted LAST CHANCE hooks. CUT: any face test this cycle. PARK: spare seeds until the germination test, PARK: recipient follow-up until Legal's consent wording is back. KEEP: everything else, trimmed to its smallest version that still ships. Objections now or never.'

decisions.text: Scope cuts: CUT pot-in-box, CUT shouted 'last chance' hooks, CUT founder-face test this cycle; PARK spare seeds (until germination test), PARK recipient follow-up (until consent wording reviewed); KEEP all other fixes at smallest shippable version

content: Research hands over a single typed page. 'Final test list, with pass/fail rules written in advance. Waitlist A/B with and without the remedy line. Hands vs mystique creative. Three hook variants. Two framing cuts. Buyer-type question. Bloom-or-not follow-up. Ten buyer calls. Germination test. Timed painting pilot. All measured on signups or real outcomes. No views, no likes.'

proposals.text: Pre-registered test list with pass/fail rules: remedy-line A/B, hands vs mystique, 3 hook variants, 2 framing cuts, buyer-type question, bloom-or-not follow-up, 10 buyer calls, germination test, timed painting pilot; metrics = signups or real outcomes only

content: Brand glances at the LAST CHANCE note on the floor, then at Growth. 'I know you'll bring that back. For the record, I'll fight it again.' Growth shrugs: 'For the record, I'll bring it back if the live count test wins.'
disagreement: Brand vs Growth on shouted urgency remains open beyond this cycle

content: The Designer trims their own row. 'Smallest version of F1 and F8: the lid card only. One card, two sides, matching number. No booklet, no sticker set, no extra insert. I'll have a printed proof and a quote within a week.'
The Plant Specialist accepts the park. 'Spare seeds can wait. If the germination test comes back weak, I'll bring them back to you with the test result attached, not an opinion.'
Growth turns to Finance. 'One ask. A small paid boost so the A/B tests get enough traffic. Organic alone might not give Research enough signups to read.'

proposals.text: Small, capped paid boost to give the waitlist tests enough traffic (amount to be set by Finance; flagged as spend)
proposals.test: enough signups per variant to read the tests

content: Community accepts the cut on faces without arguing, but asks for one line in the minutes. 'Face test: cut for this cycle, not cancelled. Revisit after hands vs mystique reports.'

CX raises the size exchange one more time. 'If exchanges are subject to stock, the remedy promise has to say exactly that, in plain words, so nobody is surprised. I still think we should hold a few spare tees in common sizes, but I'll log it as my open item.'
disagreement: CX (hold spare tees for exchanges) vs Ops (exchanges only if stock exists) - open

content: Ops softens a little. 'When the checkout size data comes in, if one size clearly dominates, I'll order a couple of spares of that size. Data first. Fair?'

Finance agrees with conditions. 'A boost: yes, small, capped, a hard stop amount I set, and only on the test reels. On the damage refund, I'll sign it now with a review after Archive 002, as long as Ops logs every damaged unit. I'd rather learn the rate than keep blocking CX.'

decisions.text: Finance approves a small capped paid boost for test reels only (cap set by Finance), and signs the damage replace-or-refund line with a post-Archive 002 review, conditional on Ops logging every damaged unit

content: Legal: 'Exchanges subject to stock is fine if it's said clearly before purchase. It goes in the combined review pack. Verify with a professional.'
